items.title: Two babies killed in fire accident at newborn care ward of Telangana govt hospital
items.summary: Two babies were killed in a fire accident at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) ward of a government hospital in Telangana’s Adilabad on Monday, September 21. One of the victims was reportedly a preterm baby on ventilator care. Hospital staff and family members were seen rushing out of the ward in distress, holding the babies. Adilabad district Collector Rajarshi Shah told the media there were at least 27 babies in the SNCU of the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) Adilabad at the time of the tragedy. The surviving infants were moved to private hospitals, he said. The fire broke out around 11.40 pm on the night of September 21. The Collector said that, according to preliminary findings, a blast involving an air conditioner may have triggered the fire, filling the ward with smoke. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be determined. Additional Collector Rajeshwar said that some of the hospital staff broke the glass walls of the ward to bring the babies out. Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry into the causes of the incident. He also instructed officials that safety measures be strengthened across all hospitals to prevent the recurrence of such incident

items.title: TN: Man who set woman ablaze at Ponneri hospital shot in the leg by police
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A day after a woman contract worker was set ablaze at the Ponneri Government Hospital in Tiruvallur district, the police shot the alleged perpetrator in the leg while attempting to apprehend him near Chennai’s Madhavaram. The accused, identified as Prakash (35), allegedly poured petrol on Rajeshwari (24), a temporary worker at the hospital, and set her on fire on the evening of Monday, September 21. Rajeshwari sustained over 48% burns and was shifted to the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital in Chennai for further treatment. According to reports, a special team formed under Ponneri Inspector Sivakumar to trace Prakash located him in the Madhavaram area early Tuesday, September 22. The police are said to have surrounded him in an attempt to apprehend him when he allegedly tried to flee and attacked sub-inspector Tamizharasan. Inspector Sivakumar then opened fire, hitting Prakash in the leg. He was subsequently apprehended and admitted to a nearby government hospital for treatment under police surveillance. The attack on Rajeshwari took place at around 7.15 pm on Monday, when she was leaving the Ponneri Government Hospital

items.title: Bengaluru court bars review bombing of movie 'The Paradise' ahead of its release
items.summary: A Bengaluru civil court has granted a temporary injunction restraining social media platform X Corp and other online entities from hosting or disseminating targeted, derogatory content against the upcoming film The Paradise ahead of its worldwide theatrical release. In an order passed on September 19, Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge observed that the film's producer, Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Cinemas LLP (plaintiff) has established a prima facie case, warranting an interim injunction. This was after the producer flagged certain online material which the Court concluded had crossed the line of fair criticism. “The documents produced indicate the propagation of derogatory statements which go beyond standard artistic evaluation and appear targeted to diminish the commercial value of the production,” the Court observed. The order was passed in an application moved under the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) by the the plaintiff suit seeking permanent and mandatory injunction against X Corp and others. The counsel for the plaintiff submitted that substantial investments were made in the production, marketing, and distribution of the movie, which is scheduled for theatrical release
